source.title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
source.summary: The Amazon rainforest is a crucial buffer against climate change - but deforestation had expanded under former president Jair Bolsonaro.
source.evidence_text:
The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.
During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, news agency AFP reported, citing official data.
Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue.
Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.
"Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday.
Left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.
Lula reversed his policies and oversaw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office. Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging.
Jair Bolsonaro promoted mining in indigenous lands in the Amazon and forest clearances soared at the same time as resources to protect the forest were cut.
Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.
Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species. In a healthy state, they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool.
It showed that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said.
But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires.

grammar.concept: Participle clauses for result or simultaneous action
grammar.example_quote: In a healthy state, these tropical expanses assimilate massive volumes of carbon dioxide, mitigating planetary heating while sheltering millions of distinct species.
grammar.explanation: Writers often use a present participle (an "-ing" verb) after a comma to describe the result of the main action or something happening at the same time. In this sentence, "mitigating planetary heating" is a direct result of the tropical expanses absorbing carbon dioxide, and "sheltering" introduces an additional simultaneous function.

news_brief_sentences: Ahead of a fiercely contested presidential run-off in which the ecosystem's future is a key issue, the Brazilian government reports that deforestation rates have fallen to record lows.
Satellite data reveals that the deforestation rate in the Amazon plummeted by 41.8 percent over a twelve-month period, marking the most substantial drop since systematic records began in 1988.
Given that sixty percent of this vast ecosystem lies within Brazilian borders, the region functions as an indispensable buffer against the worsening impacts of global climate change.
In a healthy state, these tropical expanses assimilate massive volumes of carbon dioxide, mitigating planetary heating while sheltering millions of distinct species.
Nevertheless, the biome faces relentless pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance driven by expanding agriculture and logging operations.
This ecological degradation intensified under former president Jair Bolsonaro, when the Amazon endured a loss of forest lands that exceeded the previous four-year period by nearly sixty percent.
This extensive destruction unfolded as the previous administration promoted mineral extraction in indigenous territories and simultaneously cut resources designed to safeguard the forest.
President Lula definitively reversed his predecessor's policies, instituting rigorous environmental oversight and tightening consequences to suppress illicit logging.
One climate advocate observed that this subsequent turnaround demonstrates how, given sufficient political will, it is entirely possible to curb deforestation alongside greenhouse gas emissions.

However, with polls indicating a neck-and-neck race, Lula will soon confront Bolsonaro's son Flavio, who is widely anticipated to continue his father's policies should he secure victory, although he has explicitly pledged to combat organized crime in the Amazon.
lesson.overview: Amid a tightly contested presidential race, Brazil has achieved a substantial reduction in Amazon deforestation, highlighting the stark environmental impacts of differing political administrations.
